> **What you can defend when you leave.** Decide how you and your tools will work before there is anything at stake, so the rules exist when the pressure arrives.

## What this studio produces

A responsibility statement naming what you will never delegate, your AI and data-handling rules, your opened AI Research Ledger, and an early red-flag screen of your project idea.

This is a **versioned checkpoint**, not a pass. You date it, number it, and
attach the reason for the version. When later evidence changes it, you write
the next version rather than editing the last one, because the sequence of
changes is itself part of your research record.

## The practice {#checkpoint}

1. Write your responsibility statement: the decisions that stay yours no matter how good the tool gets.
2. Write your AI working rules: what you will delegate, what you will always verify, and how you will record both.
3. Open your AI Research Ledger and enter your first row, today, for any tool you have already used on this project.
4. Run the red-flag screen on your idea: is it answerable, is it yours to ask, and could you defend attempting it.

## The four rails, here

Four concerns cross every studio in this book. At this studio they take
these specific forms.

- **Ethics, permissions, and data exposure.** State now what data you expect to touch, so the ethics studio has something to check against.
- **Evidence, provenance, and reproducibility.** Decide where your project's files will live before you have any.
- **AI activity, verification, and human decisions.** This studio opens the ledger every other studio appends to.
- **Uncertainty, claim boundary, and revision history.** Write what you currently believe about your question, so later revisions are visible as revisions.

## What sends you back

Any change in your tools, your data source, or your collaborators sends you back here for a new version.

## How this checkpoint is assessed

Each row scores **0**, **1**, or **2**. **10 points total.**

| # | Criterion | 0 | 1 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The station's artifact exists in full, specific to your own project | absent, or generic text that would fit any project | present but incomplete, or specific in some parts and generic in others | complete and unmistakably about your project |
| 2 | The checkpoint is written as a dated, numbered version with its reason | no version, or a version with no reason given | versioned, but the reason is decorative rather than an account of what changed | versioned with a reason a reader could use to reconstruct your thinking |
| 3 | Every judgment in the artifact is defended by you, not asserted by a tool | conclusions appear with no reasoning, or reproduce a tool's wording | reasoning present but thin where the decision was hardest | each judgment carries a reason you could defend under questioning |
| 4 | The four rails are carried in this station's specific form | one or more rails absent where this station required them | all rails present but one is nominal | every rail addressed in the form this station requires |
| 5 | The station's own product is present and defensible: A responsibility statement naming what you will never delegate, your AI and data-handling rules, your opened AI Research Ledger, and an early red-flag screen of your project idea | the station's own product is missing | present but would not survive a careful question | present and defensible as stated |
